name: Media Capabilities
plain: Which video and audio formats decode smoothly and power-efficiently on this device.
meaning: Reveals hardware decoder generation, HDR support and codecs (AV1, HEVC, VP9, Dolby) and so GPU and OS tier. Sites use it to pick streams; it also fingerprints the device.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can ask how well your device plays each video and audio format
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a video page or player loads
can: Check which formats play smoothly and save battery
Check for HDR and codec support such as AV1, HEVC, or Dolby
Pick the best stream for your screen
Guess your graphics tier from the answers
cannot: See your videos or watch history
Ask about formats the browser does not know
Change how your device plays video

story.what_it_is: Tells a page which video and sound formats play smoothly and use little battery on your device.

marketing.name: Media Capabilities API
marketing.pitch: Docs describe it as a way for sites to choose smooth, power-friendly streams.

marketing.name: Media Capabilities on web.dev
marketing.pitch: Chrome teams say it helps sites pick the best video quality for each device.

story.for_you: You never see it. It helps your video start in the best quality your device can really play, without stutter or a hot laptop. The cost is that the answers also say a lot about your hardware.
story.for_makers: Streaming sites use it to choose between formats like AV1, HEVC and VP9 and to avoid choppy video. It reveals decoder generation, HDR and GPU tier. That makes it useful to measure users and to fingerprint them.

use_cases.example: A streaming site picks 4K HDR for a TV-class display and 1080p for a basic laptop.
A video site chooses AV1 only on devices with a hardware decoder, to save battery.
A cloud gaming site picks the stream format that your device decodes smoothly for low delay.
A live sports stream drops to a simpler format on a phone that cannot decode the best one smoothly.
A video call app selects an encoder that will not overheat your device.
A video ad server picks a creative format your device decodes without lag.
A fingerprint vendor reads the decoder answers to tell GPU generations apart.

technical_bounds: Answers per queried configuration; nothing listed upfront
Cannot enumerate all codecs at once
